stages.headline: a − b is the vector that gives a when added to b; if a = OA and b = OB then a − b = BA.
stages.headlineEnglish: a − b is the vector that gives a when added to b; if a = OA and b = OB then a − b = BA.

stages.headline: The opposite vector −a has the same modulus and the opposite direction: a + (−a) = 0 and a − b = a + (−b).
stages.headlineEnglish: The opposite vector −a has the same modulus and the opposite direction: a + (−a) = 0 and a − b = a + (−b).

stages.headline: Examples: in a parallelogram AB − AD = DB; in a cube AC₁ − AA₁ = A₁C₁.
stages.headlineEnglish: Examples: in a parallelogram AB − AD = DB; in a cube AC₁ − AA₁ = A₁C₁.
